Source unchanged since 2026.10.29.2. Refused before any crane call or write: a source that does not become a repository path (Foo/bar, LocalHost/x, [::1]:5000/x, ghcr.io/Team/Hello); and two sources of one run at one target or one mirror record name (docker.io/nats:2.10 + docker.io/library/nats:2.10; ghcr.io/foo-bar/baz:v1 + ghcr.io/foo/bar-baz:v1). The first is still tested through sourcePath; the second, the in-run collision refusal, lost its unit test with the fake and is now untested (see testing-completeness). A target registry that refuses deep paths (Docker Hub) still fails only at crane copy time, as README.md says.

Reviewed the new registry_test.ts against 5c05905. The fake crane over a fake registry is gone; each of the five methods (digest, describe, copy, tag, blob) runs through createModelTestContext with a stub exec at __setExec that answers only the argument prefixes its test lists and rejects any other call, restored in a finally. Each method has a success test asserting the record's spec, name and fields (digest also uses storedResources to check previousDigest and changed) and a failure test asserting the error and an empty write list. copy checks the password reaches crane on stdin only, is not in the arguments, the records or the log, and that DOCKER_CONFIG is a run-own directory. The pure parts (references, the arguments check, tar reading with pax and GNU long names) keep their tests. deno task test: 18 passed, 1 ignored (opt-in e2e). Thinner than before: the refusal of two sources colliding on one target, which the previous review relied on under error-handling, is no longer pinned by a unit test, and no failure path plants the password. Not blocking for a release whose source is unchanged; worth one test each later. README's new test paragraph matches the file.

2026.11.12.1 is a tests-only release: git diff 5c05905 shows registry.ts changed only by the version and one identity upgrades entry, so this verdict stands from the review of 2026.10.29.2. Registry use is unchanged. sourcePath follows docker/distribution normalisation where it matters: a host has '.' or ':' or is 'localhost'; library/ is added only for a single-component Docker Hub path; index.docker.io and registry-1.docker.io are folded into docker.io, as documented. The '_' port separator is injective over references that the Docker/OCI reference grammar accepts, because a domain component there has no '_'. It is not injective over everything sourcePath accepts. The first component is only checked for '.' or ':', so a host holding '_' passes, and crane 0.22.1 accepts such a host too (`crane digest foo.example_5000/x:1` gets as far as a DNS lookup). Failing pair: foo.example:5000/x and foo.example_5000/x both map to foo.example_5000/x. In one run the duplicate check refuses them; across runs they share one mirror repository. A non-numeric port is also taken: a.b:c/x maps to a.b_c/x, and crane then fails on it. IPv6 hosts are refused. Low severity: such a host is invalid under RFC 1123 and refused by containerd/Docker, so no node would ever pull through that mirror path.

2026.11.12.1 is a tests-only release: git diff 5c05905 shows registry.ts changed only by the version and one identity upgrades entry, so this verdict stands from the review of 2026.10.29.2. In-run collisions are now refused (crane/registry.ts, copy's seen map). Across runs they are not: sanitized() still writes '/' and '-' both as '-'. Failing input: in one model, copy ghcr.io/foo-bar/baz:v1@d1 in one run and ghcr.io/foo/bar-baz:v1@d2 in a later run. Both write mirror-<registry>-<namespace>-ghcr.io-foo-bar-baz-v1, and the second becomes the latest version of the first's record. Assertions filtered by workflowRunId are unaffected. A reader by name is not: ko-signed-images with baseImageRecord, or data.latest(...) as the signed-images README shows, then gets the other upstream's target and digest, silently, though it is still a mirror this model signed. Low likelihood (it needs a sanitizer-ambiguous pair with the same tag in one model) and far rarer than the old layout's real target collisions on the last segment. Still a reachable wrong-record read that an injective encoding or a hash suffix would remove. digest records have had the same cross-run collision on source repositories since the first version, and there it can carry a wrong firstSeenAt into a quarantine.

2026.11.12.1 is a tests-only release: git diff 5c05905 shows registry.ts changed only by the version and one identity upgrades entry, so this verdict stands from the review of 2026.10.29.2. Unchanged: digest reads its last record through readResource. Workflows read attributes.target/repository from mirror records and build no paths. In mirror-release-images, the image and its sha256-<hex> signature tag both go through sourcePath of the same source repository, so they share a repository and cosign verify at the target finds the signature. They run as two separate copy calls with different tags, so the new in-run duplicate check does not trip between them. Pre-existing and untouched: a slashless repository in release.json would send the signature digest to the target registry and namespace while the image copy reads Docker Hub.
